sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: Official UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression for Russia (June 2025): concludes that LGBT+ people in general do not face a real risk of persecution or serious harm from the state, with three stated exceptions - the North Caucasus, trans people, and publicly active LGBT advocacy are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution; under the 'gay propaganda' law, public expression promoting non-heterosexual relationships or gender transition is punishable by administrative fines or detention of up to 15 days, with repeated offences prosecutable criminally for up to four years; the 2023 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement enables further charges; notes there is no reliable information on the size or distribution of the country's LGBT+ population.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (Cloudflare block); the underlying US State Department travel advisory for Russia warns that foreign nationals found guilty of violating the 'propaganda' law may be detained for up to 15 days and deported, flags display of symbols including the rainbow flag as a crime, and advises against all travel regardless of personal characteristic, noting government support for citizens is very limited in parts of the country.

sources.title: Russia: Rising Toll of LGBT ‘Extremism’ Designation | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch report (30 June 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for allegedly participating in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its symbols - approximately 98 for administrative (minor misdemeanour) offences and three for criminal liability - demonstrating authorities' determination to penalise LGBT expression, association and symbolism.
